title: Identification of Determinants for Variability in Mitochondrial Biochemical Complex Activities
projectDescription: Diagnosis of mitochondrial disease is based on multiple criteria, such as clinical scores (assessing muscle, central nervous system, and multisystem involvement), imaging results, biopsy histology, genome analyses and biochemical analyses of the electron transport chain complex activities. The complex activities vary strongly between healthy individuals and limits the use for diagnosis. In this project, we have evaluated posttranslational and genetic contributors to such variation in complex activities that -if corrected for- could improve diagnostic precision. We have used proteomic analyses of mitochondria to examine the degree that protein composition of the mitochondria correlates with biochemical activity of complexes as well as posttranslational and genetic factors.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Human muscle mitochondria isolated from healthy volunteers. The mitochondria were isolated by homogenization of muscle tissue and frozen in SETH (sucrose-EDTA-Tris-Heparin) buffer until thawing and subjected to MS analyses.   Proteomic analysis of isolated muscle mitochondria was performed at the Proteomic Core Facility (Department of Immunology, University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway). LC–MS/MS analysis was carried out using a nanoElute nanoflow ultrahigh pressure LC system (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) coupled with a timsTOF fleX mass spectrometer (Bruker Daltonics), using a CaptiveSpray nanoelectrospray ion source (Bruker Daltonics) as described in Stevanovic et al.  Reference: Stevanovic, A. Dalmao-Fernandez, D. Mohamed, T.A. Nyman, E. Kostovski, P.O. Iversen, M. Savikj, N. Nikolic, A.C. Rustan, G.H. Thoresen, E.T. Kase, Time-dependent reduction in oxidative capacity among cultured myotubes from spinal cord injured individuals, Acta Physiol (Oxf) 240(7) (2024) e14156.
dataProcessingProtocol: MaxQuant version 2.4.7.0 was used for the database search. MaxQuant data from samples 1, 4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 is used in the current project.
